activity.notes: Arminius, later commonly called Hermann in German tradition, was a Cheruscan war-chief/chieftain who led the anti-Roman revolt beginning in CE 9 and remained a major Cheruscan military-political leader until his death in CE 21. ATLAS does not model him as king: Oxford notes that his later attempt to establish personal tyranny/kingship met resistance. The Cherusci binding represents the historically attested tribal political authority he led, not a generic Germania polity.

sources.title: Arminius, b. c. 19 BCE — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: Oxford Classical Dictionary identifies Arminius as war-chief of the Cherusci and the leader who destroyed Varus's army in CE 9; it also describes his later Cheruscan leadership and failed aspiration to kingship.

sources.title: Arminius — Deutsche Biographie
sources.citation_text: Deutsche Biographie identifies Arminius, also known as Hermann, as a Cheruscan prince and commander and dates his death to CE 21.
